subject.title: Native Claude tool-use via can_use_tool control request is denied immediately for any exec policy except security=full+ask=off — ask=on-miss never generates an approval request

question: Should restrictive Claude live sessions relay native `can_use_tool` requests to human approval, and which approval contract should govern Bash versus non-shell tools such as Write and Read?
rationale: The expected user behavior is clear, but choosing the durable approval family, request binding, actor authorization, timeout behavior, and relationship to command-specific exec safeguards changes a security-sensitive boundary.

options.title: Add typed native approvals
options.body: Introduce a generic native-tool approval request with exact tool/input/session binding, while adapting Bash through command-aware exec safeguards where feasible.

options.title: Exec approval for Bash only
options.body: Route only Claude Bash requests through existing exec approvals and continue denying other native tools unless separately auto-allowed.

options.title: Keep restrictive denial
options.body: Retain synchronous denial outside full bypass and update documentation and release wording to state that interactive native approvals are unsupported.

recommendation.title: Add typed native approvals
recommendation.body: Introduce a generic native-tool approval request with exact tool/input/session binding, while adapting Bash through command-aware exec safeguards where feasible.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly relevant recent merged history is the Claude `can_use_tool` response-contract work credited to this contributor.
